discovery: Photonic crystals: photonic band gaps and the localization of light
subfield: Optics and photonics / condensed matter physics of waves
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures can have a complete photonic band gap. Yablonovitch showed that such a gap suppresses spontaneous emission. John showed that disorder in these structures can produce strong Anderson localization of light. Yablonovitch then built the first three-dimensional photonic crystal with a full band gap. These ideas made light a clean laboratory for solid-state wave physics: band structure, defect states, localization and, later, topological photonics, which grew directly out of this framework. Their work also showed that atom-light interaction can be engineered by controlling the electromagnetic vacuum itself, which opened up cavity and waveguide quantum electrodynamics in photonic band-gap media. The applications are real and widespread: photonic-crystal fibers, ultra-high-Q nanocavities, low-threshold nanolasers, slow-light devices and integrated silicon photonics. The concept they created gave rise to a whole field that has reshaped both optics and condensed matter physics.
